question: Pour comparer les coûts de logement d'un propriétaire et d'un locataire dans le recensement canadien, suffit-il de comparer le versement hypothécaire au loyer?
generated_answer: Le versement hypothécaire ne représente qu'une partie du coût de logement d'un propriétaire. You can compare the cost of housing for homeowners and renters by calculating the cost of housing as a percentage of household income. The Census of Population asks respondents to report their monthly housing costs. These costs include mortgage payments, property taxes and condominium fees, as well as electricity, heat, water and other municipal services. The question also asks respondents to report their monthly rent payments. The Census of Population asks respondents to report their household income. This includes income from all sources on a before-tax basis. The cost of housing can be calculated as a percentage of household income by dividing the cost of housing by household income and multiplying by 100. This calculation can be done for both homeowners and renters. The cost of housing as a percentage of household income can be compared between homeowners and renters to see if there is a difference in the cost of housing for these two groups. The Census of Population also asks respondents to report their household size. This can be used to adjust the cost of housing for homeowners and renters to account for differences in household size. For example, a household with two people may have a lower cost of housing per person than a household with four people. By adjusting the cost of housing for household size, you can get a more accurate comparison of the cost of housing for homeowners and renters.
